SWEPT 2026-08-31, all 38 cells, and the sweep EARNED ITS KEEP: it found a real defect and two real a11y gaps that twelve admissions and four sink sections had introduced since the last one.

THE DEFECT: check-runtime-classes reported dropdown--open, list-box__menu-item--highlighted and side-nav--expanded STRIPPED at load, with all three still in the file and check-coverage still counting them. js/date-picker.js adopted a markup-declared-open calendar and registered it WITHOUT dismissOthers:false, so it tore down every surface already adopted. js/list-box.js documents this exact trap in a comment written 2026-08-28; a module authored after it walked in. Fixed at f10e3ae.

THE A11Y GAPS: three fluid selects reported "no visible focus change" and were RIGHT — Carbon gates a fluid control’s ring on a class React adds on focus (select--fluid--focus and siblings) and nothing here applied it, so a fluid select took focus and painted nothing. js/form-controls.js now applies all three, on the three different hosts the selectors name.

ONE NEW FALSE POSITIVE, adjudicated: the fluid list box draws its ring on the WRAPPER and Carbon sets outline:none on the field, so check-a11y cannot see it. Measured on focus: the wrapper goes from outline none to rgb(15,98,254) solid 2px. Same family as progress-step-button, left reported.

TWO WRONG DIAGNOSES ARE ON RECORD IN f10e3ae rather than deleted, because both were plausible and both cost a measurement to kill.

PORTAL IS A FIXED POINT, and reading it mid-sweep gives a wrong answer. portal.html RENDERS this ledger -- a current cell is a tag--green, a stale one a tag--magenta -- so recording a cell changes the page the cell describes. Measured 2026-08-31: mid-sweep, with cells dirty, check-runtime-classes read 66 classes because tag--magenta was in the markup; once every cell was recorded and the portal rebuilt, it read 65 with 77 green tags and 0 magenta. READ PORTAL LAST, after the other cells are written and npm run verify has rebuilt it, or its reading records a transient state.

A SECOND ORDERING TRAP, same sweep: a cell records the HEAD commit it was taken at, and a cell whose declared inputs are MODIFIED IN THE WORKING TREE is neither current nor stale -- it is dirty, a third state. Recording 15 cells against uncommitted template edits left the summary reading "2 current, 11 stale" out of 35, with 22 cells in neither bucket. COMMIT THE CHANGE FIRST, THEN STAMP THE CELLS. The readings themselves were valid; only the stamp was premature.

SWEPT 2026-08-31 at 349a68c, 24 of 35 cells. Every reading either reproduced its recorded value EXACTLY or moved by an amount traceable to a change made the same day -- sink/card.html, and the h3-to-p heading fix in wizard-page and the portal generator. Nothing moved that should not have.

THE ELEVEN check-a11y CELLS WERE NOT SWEPT AND ARE STILL STALE. The automated pane reports document.visibilityState "hidden" and document.hasFocus() false, and neither can be changed from inside the page -- window.focus() and body.focus() do not move it. check-a11y refuses its focus-ring half in that state BY DESIGN, and gates.mjs records the precondition: a 0 with focusRingChecked:false is not a pass. Recording one would have produced a cell that looks swept and is not, which is the exact failure this ledger exists to prevent. They need a human with a focused window.

THE OTHER FOUR GATES ARE SOUND IN A HIDDEN PANE, and that is evidenced rather than assumed: layout computes normally (card measured 297x212 with a real background), and eleven independent readings reproduced values a person had taken in a visible browser. Where a gate depends on a state a hidden pane cannot reach, it says so itself -- which is why only check-a11y is missing.
